ODDLY MADRAS · SS'26
01 — Opening

A collection,
made real together.

It begins as feedback and ends as something people own.

The shape of it

A collection is tested, then celebrated.

Every Oddly Madras collection moves through two kinds of gathering — one that happens before it reaches the world, and one that happens again and again once it has. The first listens. The second sells. What follows is how each works, and how they hand off to each other.

A design begins on an iPad and, at best, meets a mannequin. Neither wears it. Fitlab is where the upcoming collection first touches real bodies — a small room of invited people who try the prototypes and tell us what they feel. It is a working session dressed as an evening.

Bloom Room comes later, and repeats. Once the collection is real, we bring people into a styled room built around it and we sell. Where Fitlab asks a question, Bloom Room makes an offer.

The two are joined by a single thread: the person who gives feedback at Fitlab is invited back to buy at a Bloom Room, discount in hand. Community becomes commerce without either feeling forced.

Feedback engine vs. revenue engine

The clearest way to hold the two formats apart is by the single thing each exists to produce. Read across.

What it produces
Fitlab produces usable feedback. Bloom Room produces revenue.
Timing
Fitlab runs before a collection launches — usually once, sometimes more in cities where our customer base runs deep. Bloom Room runs several times, across its life.
Room size
Fitlab: 10–15, closed. Bloom Room: ~20–30, invite-led — larger with a big partner.
What's on the rack
Fitlab: prototypes in set sizes. Bloom Room: the finished, purchasable collection.
What the guest leaves with
Fitlab: a sense of authorship, and a discount to use later. Bloom Room: the garment.
02 — Fitlab by Oddly

Fitlab by Oddly

A closed room of ten to fifteen people, the upcoming collection in prototype, and one job: put the clothes on real bodies and listen.

Purpose

Validation, before the market sees it.

A garment can look resolved on a screen and on a mannequin and still fail the only test that matters — a person moving through an evening in it. Fitlab exists to close that gap. We bring the upcoming collection, still in prototype, into a relaxed room and let invited people wear it, sit in it, reach across a table in it, and say what a mannequin never could.

It looks like an evening with friends. It functions as the last product checkpoint before we commit the collection to production.

  • Prototypes tested on real, varied bodies — not screens, not forms
  • The final fit and feel checkpoint before production
  • Framed as an intimate evening, run as product development
Timing

Fitlab sits at a fixed point in the calendar: before a collection launches. A new collection almost always passes through a Fitlab on its way to release — it is the gate, not a detour. Usually that means one, but where our customer base runs deep in a particular city, we’ll hold another there. How many is decided case by case.

When
Before launch of a new collection
How often
Usually once per collection — more where a city’s customer base merits it
Its role
A gate every collection passes through before production
Guest list

The room is deliberately small — ten to fifteen people — so every voice is heard and every reaction is seen. Today those seats go to friends and family: people who will be honest, who care, and who understand what they're being let into. Increasingly, they also go to people we choose on purpose — high-engagement customers, the ones already close to the brand and likely to convert. Their feedback is sharp, and the invitation deepens a relationship that's already warm.

Open question

The friends-and-family room keeps feedback candid; strategic invites — high-engagement customers with real potential to convert — widen the range of bodies and tastes without losing that honesty. How far to open the room beyond both groups is a question we keep answering edition by edition.

  • 10–15 people, closed invite
  • Friends and family, plus high-engagement customers chosen to convert
  • Small enough that every reaction is legible
Format & setting

Fitlab is held in a café or another closed, informal space — never a store, never a showroom. The ease of the setting is the point: people relax, and relaxed people tell the truth. Seats are laid with feedback cards; a rail of prototypes waits to one side.

Invite mechanics

How someone is asked is decided case by case. It might be a considered PR box with goodies that makes the evening feel like an occasion, or a direct WhatsApp message to someone we know. The channel flexes; the intimacy doesn't.

PR boxWhatsApp inviteBy hand
Mechanics

Try, then tell.

Prototypes are made in set sizes — not the full range — so the evening is built around what's available to try rather than a personal fitting. Guests move through the pieces, wear what fits, and record their reactions on the cards at their seats. The feedback is the deliverable; the garment is the prompt.

Do

Capture the honest reaction — where it pulls, where it sings, what they’d never wear and why. That’s the raw material.

Don’t

Treat it as a sale or a personal fitting. Sizing is limited by design; the goal is signal, not a transaction.

Community layer

Beneath the product work, Fitlab does something quieter and just as valuable. It gives people a first, private look at what's coming, and a genuine hand in shaping it. A guest who suggests a strap change and later sees it in the collection doesn't just own the dress — they own a piece of the decision.

  • First look at the upcoming collection, before anyone else
  • A real sense of authorship in the design
  • Preorders open to those who want a piece early
Incentive

Taking part earns a discount. It's negotiated rather than fixed — a natural consequence of the friends-and-family room today — and it isn't meant to be spent on the spot. It's carried forward — redeemable at a Bloom Room, or simply on the website. Attending a second event should never feel like a condition of using it; the discount is theirs to spend wherever suits them.

Form
Negotiated, not a flat rate
Why informal
Fits the current friends-and-family guest list
Where it's spent
At a Bloom Room, or on the website — whichever suits
Constraints

Two honest limits shape the evening, and naming them keeps expectations right.

  • Not everyone tries the piece they most want — sizing is limited per prototype
  • Everyone gives feedback, whatever they were able to wear
  • Scaling the guest list wider still is a work in progress
Success metric

Fitlab is judged on the quality of what we hear, not what we sell. There's a baseline, and there's a ceiling.

Baseline success

Good, usable feedback — clear enough to change a pattern, a fabric, or a fit before production.

Exceptional success

A preorder. Someone who tried it and couldn’t wait for launch is the strongest signal a prototype can earn.

03 — Bloom Room

Bloom Room

A styled room built around the collection, twenty to thirty invited guests (more with a large partner), and one job: sell — with exclusivity and community as the air in the room.

Purpose

Closing the loop.

Bloom Room is where community and validated product turn into revenue. The collection is finished and for sale; the room is styled around it; the people in it were chosen. It can run after a launch to keep a collection moving, or before one as an exclusive first-look — the collection revealed and sold to a chosen room before it reaches anyone else. It runs more than once across a collection's life.

If Fitlab is the question, Bloom Room is the offer. Everything the earlier room learned is now on a rail, in the right sizes, ready to leave with someone.

  • Converts community and product validation into sales
  • Runs pre- or post-launch, and repeats across the collection’s life
  • The commercial engine of the cycle
Timing

Where Fitlab is a single gate, Bloom Room is a series. Several are held across one collection's lifecycle — sometimes as an exclusive first-look before launch, sometimes well after it — each aimed at a fresh room of people.

When
Across the collection’s lifecycle — from a pre-launch first-look to well after release
How many
Multiple per collection
Cadence driver
Sales targets, live demand, and remaining inventory
Guest list

Each Bloom Room holds around twenty to thirty people, and who's in the room is decided per edition. When we co-host with a larger partner brand, the room can run bigger — their audience swells it, by design. The deciding logic is data: we prioritise cities where the collection already sold well at pop-ups, and invite existing customers there back into a room built for them. New faces come by invite alongside them.

  • Around 20–30 guests per edition — larger when a big partner brings their own crowd
  • Mix of repeat and new customers, chosen case by case
  • City choice follows pop-up sales — we return where the work landed
Format & setting

Every Bloom Room is staged around a theme chosen for that moment in the collection, so no two feel identical. One edition might be runway-forward with a walk; another might be a quiet community gathering. The styling carries the theme, and the theme gives the edition its identity.

Themed per editionFashion walkCommunity meetStyling-led
Invite mechanics

Invite-only, and one door left open.

Bloom Room is not an open event. Like Fitlab, it runs on a curated, founder-led guest list — people invited on purpose, for who they are to the brand. That is what keeps the room warm and the evening intentional, and it stays that way: there is no public sign-up, no walk-in, no scramble for spots.

The one door we leave open is the plus-one. Each invited guest may bring someone with them — and we trust the guest to choose well. It is an invitation, not an obligation: bring a person who'd genuinely love this too. That single hand-off is how the room grows — slowly, and only ever through someone who already belongs in it.

As with Fitlab, the ask itself flexes to the guest — a full PR box for some, a WhatsApp message for others. The register is set by who's being invited and what the edition is trying to be.

The list
Curated and founder-led — invited on purpose, never open or walk-in
The plus-one
Each guest may bring one, and chooses who — someone who'd love it too
Why it works
Every new face arrives vouched for, so the room widens without diluting
Do

Trust the guest to bring someone who genuinely fits the room. The vouch is the filter — a plus-one is warm word-of-mouth, pre-vetted by someone who already loves the brand.

Don’t

Open the list publicly or treat the plus-one as a free-for-all. Growth here is deliberate: one guest, one hand-off, always through someone already inside the room.

Invite-onlyFounder-curatedPlus-onePR boxWhatsApp invite
Mechanics

Style it, sell it.

The collection is presented styled, not racked — shown the way it's meant to be worn. Fitlab guests redeem the discount they earned here. And increasingly the room isn't ours alone: partner brands in jewellery and accessories style alongside our pieces and sell their own work in the same space. We host and produce; they gain a curated, buying audience; each look gains dimension.

Do

Weave a partner’s pieces into how our looks are composed, so their product and ours sell each other in the same breath.

Don’t

Sideline a collaborator at a separate table. If they’re in the room, they’re in the styling.

Community layer

Commerce is the function, but the feeling is belonging. Bloom Room continues the story Fitlab began — many guests helped shape what's now for sale — and the per-edition theme and guest brands keep each room novel enough to feel like an event rather than a shop.

  • Continues the design-and-community narrative from Fitlab
  • A distinct theme gives every edition its own character
  • Guest brands add novelty and cross-audience reach
Incentive

Three things pull a guest toward a purchase: the discount carried over from Fitlab, direct access to a collection styled in front of them, and the simple pull of exclusivity — a room, a night, a set of pieces not everyone gets to see.

  • Redemption of the Fitlab discount
  • Direct purchase access to the finished collection
  • Exclusivity and community as ambient value
Constraints

The flexibility that makes Bloom Room feel fresh is also what stays open until each edition is planned.

  • Theme, styling, and format (walk vs. meet) decided per edition
  • No fixed template — each room is composed from scratch
  • Collaboration partners chosen per event, not standing
Success metric

Bloom Room is measured on two things. Revenue is the headline; new people are the close second.

First — revenue

Sales generated on the night. Bloom Room is a selling engine, and revenue is the score it is judged by first.

Second — new people

Unique faces brought into the Oddly ecosystem — through the plus-one, through a partner’s audience, through a first-look that reaches someone new. A room that sells well and grows the circle has done both its jobs.

The two reinforce each other: every new person in the room is both a sale tonight and a customer for every season after. Exclusivity and community are the air around both — the experience that makes revenue feel like belonging, not a transaction.

04 — Where This Is Headed

A room worth
arriving for.

Where Bloom Room is today is not where it is going. This is the ambition it grows toward — early, open, and deliberately unfinished.

The ambition

Longer term, Bloom Room aspires to more than a styled sale. The ambition is to make each edition a genuine social occasion — a lifestyle-led evening, built around a theme worth showing up for in its own right — so that people from aspirational circles are drawn to be in the room. The collection is still the reason it exists; the evening is what makes attending feel like a privilege rather than a purchase.

The exact shape is deliberately open — a tasting, a salon, a gathering with the right partner and the right theme — and it is early. What is settled is the direction: Bloom Room should convene rooms whose calibre reflects the brand we intend to be, where taste is the thing being curated and the guest list is one signal of it. The specifics will be refined as the format matures.

05 — The Loop

The Loop

Fitlab and Bloom Room aren't separate events. They're one cycle that turns listening into selling, and customers into collaborators.

How the handoff works

Feedback in, revenue out.

A collection enters Fitlab as a set of prototypes and a set of questions. It leaves with answers — and with a small group of people who now feel a claim on it. Those people carry a discount forward — to spend at a Bloom Room when one opens near them, or on the website whenever they like. Either way, the thread from feedback to purchase holds.

Three things travel across the gap between the rooms, and together they are the loop.

Discount
Earned at Fitlab for feedback, redeemed against a purchase — at a Bloom Room or on the website.
Community
The authorship built at Fitlab becomes the belonging that fills Bloom Room.
Data
Pop-up and feedback signals decide which cities and customers each Bloom Room is built for.
One cycle, per collection

Read as a sequence: a Fitlab opens a collection and tests it — usually one, occasionally more in our strongest cities; several Bloom Rooms then carry it through its selling life. The first room makes the product right. The rooms that follow make it sell — to the very people who helped make it right.

  • A Fitlab before launch — usually one per collection, more where a city merits it — the product is made right
  • Multiple Bloom Rooms across its life — the product is sold
  • The same people, moved from feedback to purchase, from guest to buyer
